title: Implementing Interfaces
concept: Implement interfaces for your types by providing method bodies that satisfy the interface's signatures — making your types usable with generic code.
why: Implementation is where interfaces come alive. Without implementations, interfaces are just signatures. With them, your types gain capabilities.
tips: Use impl blocks to organize related implementations — one block per interface
The compiler error for missing methods tells you EXACTLY what's needed
Implement interfaces close to either the type definition or the interface definition
Generic impl blocks let you implement an interface for infinite types at once
common_mistakes: Forgetting the 'for TypeName' part: `impl Display { ... }` is wrong
Method signature mismatch — the compiler is strict about exact matching
Implementing interface methods that don't follow the interface's intended semantics
